title: New theoretical model of the dynamic anomalies in HTc superconductors
abstract: New theoretical model of the dynamic current-voltage characteristics anomalies in HTc superconductors in slowly varying magnetic field has been proposed. The model is based on an analysis in details of the magnetic flux penetration into HTc superconducting slab in such case. The comparison of model with previous experimental data has been presented. Theoretical analysis resulting from a new solution of diffusion equation is given as well as other one based on phenomenological critical state model.
summary: This paper develops a novel theoretical model to explain dynamic anomalies in the I-V curves of High-Temperature Superconductors under changing magnetic fields. By analyzing magnetic flux penetration using diffusion equations and critical state models, the authors show that the anomalies are highly sensitive to the rate of field change and the magnitude of the transport current. This provides a powerful diagnostic tool for studying vortex dynamics in these materials.
main_problem: The paper proposes a new theoretical model to explain the dynamic anomalies observed in the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of High-Temperature Superconductors (HTc) when subjected to slowly varying magnetic fields.
main_result: The model successfully predicts the dependence of these anomalies on the magnetic field sweep rate and transport current amplitude, offering a diagnostic tool sensitive to the dynamics of magnetic flux penetration.
method: The analysis combines solving the magnetic diffusion equation with an independent analysis using the phenomenological critical state model.
model_or_system: The physical system is an HTc superconducting slab. The model analyzes magnetic flux penetration into this slab, deriving the electric field (E) under both non-saturated and saturated penetration regimes.
key_observables: Dynamic anomalies in the I-V characteristics, and the generated electric field (E).
important_parameters: Magnetic field sweep rate, transport current amplitude, and material parameters like the magnetic diffusion coefficient (D), $B_0$, $\gamma$, and $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The magnetic field is assumed to be applied perpendicular to the superconducting surface.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of anomalies on transport current (Fig. 4), magnetic field sweep rate (Fig. 5), and the influence of material parameters ($B_0,  eta, \gamma$) (Figs. 7-9).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem using measured I-V curves (Fig. 1, 3). It then develops the theoretical framework by solving the diffusion equation (Eq. 1) and deriving E (Eqs. 4, 7). Finally, it compares these results with the critical state model (Eq. 9) and demonstrates the model's predictive power across various parameter variations.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the underlying physics involves non-equilibrium dynamics, flux flow, and critical state modeling, which share mathematical parallels with understanding dissipation and dynamics in complex quantum many-body systems.
